difficulty_reason: Provider-side setup is one short form: organization settings > OAuth Apps > Add application, pick scopes, Confirm. The real work is implementing the OAuth flow in your own app, which is your code, not Supabase configuration.

approval.kind: none for the OAuth app itself; Supabase-coordinated listing for the in-Dashboard Install Integration button
approval.wait: none for the OAuth app; undocumented for the optional Install Integration listing
approval.notes: The official build guide describes creating and publishing an OAuth app with no review step anywhere, and the marketplace blog post says the integrations marketplace is open to everyone - after your submission you can share the app with your own users via your own Connect Supabase button. The optional in-Dashboard Install Integration button is not self-serve: the partner guide has you send endpoint URLs to Supabase and exchange signing keys with them manually, with no documented criteria or timeline.
approval.wait_short: none for the app; undocumented if you want the Install button

summary: One of the lighter OAuth provider setups: a single Add application form in your Supabase organization's settings, scopes chosen at creation, no documented review, and you drive users through your own Connect Supabase button. Two honest caveats: the optional in-Dashboard Install Integration button requires manual coordination with Supabase (key exchange, shared endpoints, no documented timeline), and Supabase strongly recommends PKCE for the flow.

steps.title: Open your organization's OAuth Apps settings
steps.detail: Sign in to the Supabase dashboard, open your organization's settings, and navigate to the OAuth Apps tab.

steps.title: Add the application
steps.detail: Click Add application in the upper-right, fill in the required details (including redirect URI and the scopes your integration needs - scopes are chosen here, not in the authorize request), and click Confirm.

steps.title: Publish the app
steps.detail: The build guide refers to using the OAuth flow 'once you've published your OAuth App'. The docs do not detail the exact publish control in the dashboard - treat the precise click-path as an uncertainty and follow the console's own prompts.

steps.title: Add a Connect Supabase button to your UI
steps.detail: Supabase asks that the button follow the design guidelines in its brand assets. This button is yours - no Supabase coordination needed.

steps.title: Redirect users to the authorize URL
steps.detail: Send the user to https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state, and optionally organization_slug to pre-select an org. Supabase strongly recommends PKCE (code_challenge + code_challenge_method=S256). redirect_uri and state together cannot exceed 4 kB. The old scope query parameter is deprecated - scopes come from the app configuration.

steps.title: Exchange the code and store tokens
steps.detail: On the callback, POST to https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/token as application/x-www-form-urlencoded with grant_type=authorization_code, the code, the exact same redirect_uri, and the PKCE code_verifier if used; client_id and client_secret go in the basic-auth header. Store the access and refresh tokens; refresh via the same endpoint and handle HTTP 401 (a revoked grant kills the refresh token).

requirements: A Supabase account with an organization (free tier is enough)
At least one redirect URI for the OAuth callback
A decision on which Management API scopes the integration needs (set at app creation)
PKCE support in your OAuth client (Supabase strongly recommends it)
nuances: Scopes are configured on the app, not in the authorize request - the scope query parameter is deprecated. Updating scopes later works, but existing users must re-authorize before new scopes apply to their tokens.
redirect_uri and state together cannot exceed 4 kB; dynamically generated redirect URLs are supported by encoding the target in the state parameter.
If a user revokes access, refresh tokens stop working and access tokens fail with HTTP 401 - handle that explicitly.
Supabase's docs note current limitations: only some Management API features are available to OAuth apps until fine-grained access control rolls out.
For something built only for yourself or your team, skip OAuth apps entirely - a Management API personal access token is the documented path.

common_blockers.problem: Expecting the in-Dashboard Install Integration button to be self-serve like the OAuth app itself.
common_blockers.solution: Plan for manual coordination with Supabase: the partner guide has you share endpoint URLs and exchange staging/production signing keys with them, with no documented timeline. Ship your own Connect Supabase button first - it needs no coordination.

common_blockers.problem: Adding scopes later and assuming connected users get them.
common_blockers.solution: Scope changes only apply after each user re-authorizes; version your scopes at creation and prompt re-consent when they change.

agent_can_do: Draft the registration values (name, redirect URIs, scope set)
Implement the authorize redirect, PKCE, callback and token-refresh code
Draft the Connect Supabase button against the brand guidelines
Prepare the endpoint pair (redirect record + handler) the partner flow needs
human_must_do: Create the OAuth app in the dashboard while signed in (org settings > OAuth Apps)
Store the client secret securely outside the repo
Coordinate with Supabase directly if you want the in-Dashboard Install Integration button

evidence.claim: Creating an OAuth app is a single self-serve form: organization settings > OAuth Apps tab > Add application > fill details > Confirm; no review step appears anywhere in the registration documentation.

The authorize URL is https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and state; redirect_uri + state are capped at 4 kB together; PKCE is strongly recommended; the scope query parameter is deprecated.
Token exchange is POST https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/token (form-encoded, client_id/client_secret as basic auth); revoked grants make refresh tokens fail and access tokens return HTTP 401.
Scopes are set when the OAuth app is created and can be updated later, but existing users must re-authorize for new scopes to apply.

The in-Dashboard Install Integration button requires manual coordination with Supabase: partners send their redirect endpoint URLs and exchange staging/production EC P-256 public keys and key IDs; key rotation is manual for now.
Supabase states the integrations marketplace is open to everyone and that after your submission is complete you can share the integration with your own users via your own button.
https://supabase.com/dashboard responds with HTTP 200 (client-rendered shell); creating an OAuth app requires a signed-in Supabase account with an organization.

uncertainties: Supabase publishes no explicit statement that OAuth apps need no approval; this conclusion comes from the complete absence of any review step in the official build guide.
The docs reference publishing the app but do not show the exact dashboard control for it; the precise click-path after Confirm is unverified.
The Install Integration listing has no documented criteria, cost, or timeline - coordination happens directly with Supabase.
